title: edge-telemetry-sidecar-onboarding-and-fidelity-guardrails-2026
author: Marcus Li
body:
Overview

This guide describes the recommended onboarding flow, configuration guardrails, and troubleshooting ladder for deploying the Redwood Edge Telemetry Sidecar in enterprise Dedicated and Private deployments. The sidecar provides low-latency, filtered observability from customer ingress points to Redwood's telemetry pipeline while protecting PII, maintaining metric fidelity, and ensuring bounded resource impact on tenant gateways.

Who should use this guide

- Customer Success and Solutions Engineers onboarding dedicated/private tenants with custom ingress.
- Customer Platform Engineers responsible for sidecar installation and runtime validation.
- Observability/Telemetry Engineers verifying contract compliance and SLOs.

Goals and non-goals

- Goals: ensure telemetry completeness for critical signals, protect sensitive data at the edge, limit sidecar CPU/memory to avoid contention, provide clear rollback and escalation paths.
- Non-goals: full ingestion pipeline design; this guide assumes the customer's telemetry will route to Redwood's ingestion endpoints or a validated forwarder.

Key terms

- Sidecar: the telemetry agent deployed alongside an ingress/gateway service (Kubernetes DaemonSet / per-pod sidecar).
- Fidelity: percent of expected events/metrics retained after filtering and scrubbing.
- Contract: the documented set of events/metrics/logs the customer and Redwood agree to collect.

Quickstart checklist (high level)

1) Preflight: sign the Observability Contract SOW and verify CIDR allowlist.
2) Install sidecar in a staging namespace with sample traffic.
3) Validate signature TLS and auth with Redwood ingestion.
4) Run fidelity tests (see Validation section).
5) Approve production rollout, enable sampling/PII scrubbing rules, and monitor SLOs for 72 hours.

Required artifacts from customer before install

- Ingress topology diagram (service names, pods, expected peak RPS).
- Sample event/metric schema or example payloads.
- Accepted sampling targets and privacy constraints (fields to redact).
- Network egress rules (outbound to Redwood ingestion endpoints).

Sidecar configuration guardrails

The following guardrails are mandatory for Dedicated and Private environments unless an explicit exception is approved by Security and Compliance. Each item includes a rationale and recommended default.

- TLS-only transport to Redwood (rationale: prevent eavesdropping). Default: enforce mTLS, TLS 1.2+ with cert pinning.
- Max CPU per sidecar: 0.25 cores (rationale: avoid noisy neighbor on gateway pod). Default: request=100m, limit=250m.
- Max memory per sidecar: 256Mi (rationale: KV cache and buffers). Default: request=128Mi, limit=256Mi.
- Bounded local buffer: 10MB per sidecar, backpressure to client after buffer reach (rationale: avoid OOM and loss during downstream outages).
- PII redaction pipeline: apply schema-driven scrubbing before any logs/attributes leave the sidecar (rationale: regulatory compliance).
- Default sampling: 100% for error/latency traces, 10% for standard request traces, configurable per-route.
- Schema validation: drop fields that fail schema contract and emit a validation_error metric.

Example sidecar config snippet (kubernetes manifest fragment)

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: telemetry-sidecar-config
data:
  sidecar.yaml: |
    transport:
      endpoint: https://telemetry-ingest.redwood.example
      tls: { enable: true, mTLS: true }
    resources:
      requests: { cpu: "100m", memory: "128Mi" }
      limits:   { cpu: "250m", memory: "256Mi" }
    buffer:
      max_bytes: 10485760
    sampling:
      default_trace_rate: 0.10
      error_trace_rate: 1.0
    pii_scrub_rules:
      - path: $.request.user.email
        action: redaction
      - path: $.request.body.credit_card
        action: drop

Validation and acceptance tests (executable steps)

1) Connectivity and auth (owner: customer-platform / Redwood Oncall)
   - curl -v --cert client.crt --key client.key https://telemetry-ingest.redwood.example/health should return 200.
2) TLS verification (owner: customer-platform)
   - Check peer certificate CN matches expected.
3) Resource containment (owner: customer-platform)
   - Deploy load generator with 50% of expected peak RPS for 10 minutes. Confirm sidecar resource usage <= configured limits.
4) Fidelity smoke tests (owner: customer-success)
   - Send 1,000 synthetic requests with seeded IDs. Confirm at least 995 IDs (>=99.5%) are observed in Redwood ingestion indexing within 30s.
   - For error conditions (50 injected 5xx responses), confirm all error traces arrive (100% capture).
5) PII scrubbing test (owner: customer-security)
   - Send payloads including known PII fields. Verify those fields are redacted/dropped in the ingested payloads.
6) Backpressure behavior (owner: eng-sre)
   - Simulate downstream outage by blocking egress; confirm sidecar exposes an http 429 to upstream when buffer > 80% and recovers when egress is restored.

SLOs and acceptance criteria

- Telemetry completeness: 99.5% of contract-required events are delivered to Redwood ingestion within 30s (measured per hour).
- Ingest latency: 95th percentile <= 2s from event emission to ingestion acknowledgment.
- Sidecar CPU: < 60% of configured limit under normal peak.
- PII leakage incidents: 0 per 90-day window.

Monitoring and dashboards

Required metrics to publish to the tenant's dashboard (suggested panel names):

- sidecar.event_delivery.success_rate (panel: "Telemetry Delivery Rate")
- sidecar.buffer.usage_bytes (panel: "Sidecar Buffer")
- sidecar.tls.handshake_failures (panel: "TLS Failures")
- sidecar.pii.redaction.count (panel: "PII Redactions")
- sidecar.validation.error_rate (panel: "Schema Validation Errors")

Alerting thresholds (examples)

- P0: sidecar.event_delivery.success_rate < 95% for 5m — page on-call SRE and Customer Success.
- P1: sidecar.buffer.usage_bytes > 80% for 10m — create incident and notify customer platform.
- P2: sidecar.tls.handshake_failures > 5 per minute for 5m — notify security and review cert rotation.

Rollback and canary strategy

- Canary Deployment: 1% of production pods for 30m, validate SLOs, increase to 10% for 1h, then 30% for 2h before full rollout.
- Fast rollback criteria (automated): any P0 alert or buffer > 95% for 5m should trigger an automated rollback to prior sidecar image config.
- Manual rollback: Customer Success must coordinate with customer platform and SRE; use documented runbook: "kubectl rollout undo" command and confirm traffic stability for 15 minutes.

Troubleshooting ladder (ordered)

1) Symptom: No telemetry received from tenant
   - Check sidecar pod status (kubectl get pods -n <ns> -l app=telemetry-sidecar).
   - Review sidecar logs for TLS errors and auth failures.
   - Confirm egress firewall rules include telemetry ingestion endpoints.

2) Symptom: High validation_error metrics
   - Compare incoming payloads to agreed contract. If contract has changed, route to Solutions for schema versioning.
   - If unexpected fields appear frequently, add transformation rule in sidecar config and patch via ConfigMap.

3) Symptom: PII observed in Redwood ingestion
   - Immediately circuit the pipeline: switch sidecar to fail-closed mode (drop all logs) and open an incident (see Escalation matrix).
   - Collect impacted sample messages and perform forensics with Security.
   - Temporary mitigation: enable additional regex-based scrub rules applied server-side until sidecar rule can be patched.

Escalation matrix (who to call)

- First contact: Customer Success Engineer (CSE) assigned to account — slack: #cse-<customer>-oncall
- If unresolved in 15 minutes: Observability Engineer (obs-eng) — slack: #obs-oncall
- If PII or regulatory exposure suspected: Security Incident Response — pager: sec-incident-pager and notify legal.
- If sidecar resource exhaustion threatens production: SRE pager.

Post-deployment ops and QBR inputs

For the first QBR after onboarding, Customer Success should prepare the following artifacts:

- Telemetry fidelity report (30/60/90-day buckets) showing delivery rate, latency, and redaction counts.
- Incident log summarizing any sidecar-related alerts, root cause, and mitigations.
- Resource utilization trend across the tenant's gateway fleet.
- Proposed optimizations (e.g., tune sampling or move heavy traces to async export).

Ownership and contacts

- Customer Success (primary owner for onboarding): Marcus Li (marcus@redwood.example)

Appendix A: Example fidelity test harness (shell)

# Produce 1k synthetic requests and record delivery IDs
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  id="test-$(date +%s)-$i"
  curl -s -X POST https://tenant-ingress.example/endpoint -d \"{\\\"id\\\":\\\"$id\\\",\\\"payload\\\":\\\"ping\\\"}\" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' &
done

# Query Redwood ingestion index (pseudo-API)
curl -s 'https://telemetry-api.redwood.example/search?tag=test' | jq '.hits | length'

Appendix B: Common exceptions and approvals

- Exception: Sidecar memory limit to 512Mi for heavy enrichment workloads. Approval required from SRE and Security with signed risk assessment.
- Exception: Sampling set to 100% for premium onboarding windows (72 hours) — document and timebox in the contract.
